observed_mechanisms: Local OTLP/HTTP receiver on 127.0.0.1:4318 for metrics, logs and traces endpoints
Metrics and logs are parsed into local storage; current trace handler explicitly accepts trace payloads but does not use/store them
Provider-specific configuration enables OTLP export for supported agents
Claude tool_result/tool_decision streams are reconciled using upstream tool_use_id for approval-rate accounting
Local session/process scraping supplements telemetry for context usage, process state, RSS, ports and orphan detection
DuckDB is used as a seven-day local metrics store
agenttop.privilege_boundary: No eBPF/root requirement for normal OTLP receiver operation; however setup mutates provider configuration and some local hooks/files, so it is lower-privilege rather than zero-intervention.
agenttop.causal_boundary: Most semantic evidence originates from provider-emitted telemetry or local scraping. It is not an independent system-boundary witness of file/network/process effects and cannot mint F2 causal_id, generation, effect_id or completion truth.
agenttop.current_trace_gap: The current /v1/traces handler is a no-op beyond accepting the request, so agenttop cannot presently supply a complete trace-based causal spine merely because upstream agents emit OTLP traces.
agenttop.storage_boundary: agenttop DuckDB is derived observability storage only; importing it as canonical F2 state would violate UnifiedDB authority.

agentsight.strength: Can observe process/file/network/resource activity from outside the application via eBPF/TLS/system capture and therefore can disagree with self-reported application telemetry.
costs: Linux/kernel and privilege requirements for full eBPF capture
TLS attachment/version fragility and partial-visibility fallbacks
heuristic correlation cannot be upgraded to exact F2 causal identity

otlp.finding: OTLP traces, metrics and logs are stable transport signals over gRPC or HTTP; OTLP/HTTP defines /v1/traces, /v1/metrics and /v1/logs and request/response delivery semantics.
otlp.f2_implication: F2 can distill a small standards-based OTLP ingress without adopting agenttop's TUI or DuckDB, but transport acceptance is not semantic or causal truth.

genai_semconv.source: OpenTelemetry semantic-conventions current registry / GenAI migration surface
genai_semconv.finding: GenAI attributes and tool-call semantics remain a moving compatibility surface and may carry sensitive content; tool call identifiers are useful source identifiers but do not equal F2 effect authority.
genai_semconv.f2_implication: Pin semantic-convention versions and keep raw provider identifiers as provenance fields unless exact F2 bindings exist.

comparative_findings.finding: agenttop is materially lower privilege and more portable than AgentSight for provider-emitted telemetry, but it observes a weaker epistemic layer because its main semantic stream is emitted by the agent/provider itself.

AgentSight and agenttop are complementary rather than interchangeable: agenttop is strongest for low-friction tool/token/provider telemetry; AgentSight is strongest where independent system-boundary evidence is the discriminator.

The full agenttop application should not be imported merely to receive OTLP. A thin F2-native OTLP adapter can reuse the standard protocol/semantic ideas while preserving UnifiedDB and F2 evidence authority.
The current agenttop trace endpoint is not sufficient for F2 causal trace closure because it intentionally accepts traces without storing or processing them.

Neither observer may synthesize missing F2 causal_id/generation/effect_id from time proximity, PID, session identity, tool_use_id or correlation confidence. Missing exact bindings remain UNKNOWN/null and are declared in the run package.

proposed_two_tier_witness_pattern.tier_0: F2 native typed telemetry + UnifiedDB evidence + EffectGate/EffectJournal remain canonical authority.
proposed_two_tier_witness_pattern.tier_1_normal: Minimal F2-native OTLP ingress for provider-emitted logs/metrics/traces where available, content-minimized by default, exact upstream ids preserved as provenance only.
proposed_two_tier_witness_pattern.tier_2_diagnostic: Pinned AgentSight sidecar/offline witness only for controlled falsification/diagnostic runs that need independent process/file/network/system evidence; secret-free fixtures and explicit privilege/privacy fences required.
proposed_two_tier_witness_pattern.reason: This preserves low operational cost for routine observation while retaining a genuinely independent witness when self-report disagreement is the question.

counterhypotheses.statement: F2-native telemetry alone already provides all decision-relevant coverage, so both external witness tiers add only duplication.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: A controlled workload where either OTLP-native or system-boundary witness detects a true event/root cause missing from F2-native telemetry.

counterhypotheses.statement: A thin native OTLP ingress is more maintenance burden than simply importing agenttop.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: Source/build measurement shows direct agenttop adoption has lower dependency, compatibility and integration cost while preserving F2 authority and schema guarantees.

counterhypotheses.statement: AgentSight's privilege/privacy costs dominate its incremental independent evidence value.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: E3/E4 diagnostic A/B shows unique high-value root-cause/effect observations at bounded overhead and with zero secret leakage under the controlled fixture.

next_discriminator.objective: E3 standards-native fixture before any build candidate
next_discriminator.plan: On an admitted FREE isolated surface, feed deterministic secret-free OTLP logs/metrics plus one trace fixture through a minimal parser/adapter and compare exact F2 event/provenance mapping against agenttop behavior; separately reserve AgentSight for a later independent-system-witness A/B. No real external effect is required.
measure: unknown-id preservation without synthetic causal joins
